sentences.text: Brand was jailed this week after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault A discussion over a staggered age of consent is to take place, the work and pensions secretary has said, as the government faces calls to change the law following the case against Russell Brand.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Pat McFadden said that "appalling" stories of "abuse of power by powerful men" have emerged this week.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: A woman who alleges she was raped by jailed comedian Brand when she was 16 is now campaigning to see the law changed so that relationships between 16 and 17-year-olds and adults would be illegal.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: Questions over a staggered age of consent have "been raised and will be discussed" McFadden said, adding: "[I] can't tell you what the conclusion of that would be, but the last week has certainly put that up in lights." Adults of any age are legally able to have sex with 16 and 17-year-olds, under UK law.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: Mia Latter, who has waived her right to anonymity, told the Sunday Times that she wants the age of consent to be staggered.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: Latter is one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023 as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: Brand denied the allegations at the time and none of the six women were complainants in Brand's recent criminal trial.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: At Southwark Crown Court on Monday, Brand was sentenced to 10-and-a-half-years imprisonment after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, involving four women between 2004 and 2009.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: He was acquitted of two counts of rape and one allegation of attempted indecent assault.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: Latter said she was 16 when she met the comedian, then 30.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: She told the Sunday Times: "I think people were so struck by my story because of the age difference and the clear imbalance [in power].
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: "I don't want to criminalise teenagers having sex with each other.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: "If you're between the ages of 16 and 18, it seems reasonable that you can have relationships with each other, and [teenagers] are always going to.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: She told the paper she was "devastated" by the decision and that police had said  they didn't want the trial "to become 'the Alice show'", a reference to her pseudonym in the stories published in 2023.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: It is understood the Met Police has apologised for the language officers used in a meeting with Latter about her case.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: A Met spokesperson said: "This investigation remains ongoing.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: We understand the delay has been distressing for this victim-survivor.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: However, our focus has been on putting forward the best possible evidence." Layla Stone, founder of the campaign group Close the Consent Gap, said bringing in a staggered age of consent was about addressing a "power imbalance" in relationships involving 16 and 17 year-olds and adults.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: She urged ministers to commit to such a change.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: Stone, a child protection social worker, told the BBC that 16 and 17 year-olds were seen as children in "every single framework of the law" and "we don't believe [they are] old enough to consent to having sex with much older adults".
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: Close the Consent Gap is proposing that 16 year-olds would not be able to have a sexual relationship with anyone older than 19, and that someone aged 17 would be prohibited from a relationship with anyone older than 20.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: Further allegations of sexual misconduct in the entertainment industry came in the same week Brand was convicted.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: ITV News and the Guardian published a story alleging that comedian David Walliams had been accused of sexual misconduct by several women.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: One woman said she now characterises her alleged encounter with Walliams at 15 years old as a "sexual assault".
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: Walliams strongly denied he had any sexual contact with the girl.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: Other women alleged inappropriate behaviour when he was a judge at ITV's Britain's Got Talent, such as inviting girls and young women to his dressing room.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: Walliams said he rejected any allegations of criminal activity and that he has never engaged in the grooming of young women.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: The Metropolitan Police said on Friday it has launched an investigation into Walliams over reports of "alleged serious sexual offences", after the ITV News and the Guardian story.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: The Met said that the allegations it is investigating are separate from those reported by ITV and the Guardian but that it was "also proactively reviewing that reporting".
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: Whately said she has teenage daughters and would be concerned if they brought home a man many years older than them.
sentences.article_title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says

sentences.text: She said "other laws are failing to prevent them from being sexually exploited", adding: "Even though they are over the age of consent, young people are still entitled to be protected from harm." sentences.text: Bahrain's military said its air defence systems intercepted and destroyed the Iranian air attacks "before they could achieve their objectives".

sentences.text: The officials described the strikes as limited and defensive, and said they were in response to the IRGC firing on a US aircraft.

sentences.text: Moments after matching Colin Montgomerie's record of season-long European tour titles on Sunday, the Northern Irishman was asked about the health of his father.

sentences.article_title: Tearful McIlroy dedicates record-equalling win to ill dad

sentences.article_title: Tearful McIlroy dedicates record-equalling win to ill dad

sentences.article_title: Tearful McIlroy dedicates record-equalling win to ill dad

sentences.text: But he appears to be playing and talking with a little more freedom in recent years - the sort of freedom that comes as a result of finally completing the career Grand Slam and winning successive Masters titles - and leads to declarations of winning 10, or more.
sentences.article_title: Tearful McIlroy dedicates record-equalling win to ill dad

sentences.text: "Winning eight Order of Merits (Race to Dubai titles) was never in my list of goals growing up," said McIlroy, who closed with a bogey-free 67 to finish on 10 under and must surely now be considered Europe's greatest golfer.
sentences.article_title: Tearful McIlroy dedicates record-equalling win to ill dad

sentences.article_title: Tearful McIlroy dedicates record-equalling win to ill dad

sentences.article_title: Tearful McIlroy dedicates record-equalling win to ill dad

sentences.article_title: Tearful McIlroy dedicates record-equalling win to ill dad

sentences.article_title: Tearful McIlroy dedicates record-equalling win to ill dad

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Pat McFadden refuses to rule out that some young people might lose benefits The work and pensions secretary has backed the idea that the government should legally guarantee young people help to get into employment.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: Pat McFadden told the BBC that job support should be given a "legislative underpinning", adding the level of assistance on offer was currently "vague".
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: McFadden also confirmed that some current benefit claimants would see their current entitlement to benefits reduced when they are reassessed.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: But his Conservative counterpart Helen Whately said the idea of legally guaranteeing support "doesn't make sense" and ministers should focus instead on reducing taxes paid by employers.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: It comes ahead of a long-awaited review by former Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn, which will recommend on Tuesday that under-25s should be guaranteed job placements or training to help them find permanent work.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: His report is also expected to say that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of UK-wide universal credit - or personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to health conditions, under the plans.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: Speaking to Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Milburn said the government should divert money away from the benefits system to boost work support, adding he wanted to see "billions" extra spent on help over the next decade.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: However, the idea of reducing the entitlement of existing benefit claimants could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who scuppered a previous benefits-cutting plan under Sir Keir Starmer last year.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: Milburn said the reduced entitlement for some should be accompanied by a new "duty on government" to provide jobs support to young people, such as apprenticeships, college places, job coaching, or a job.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: He added that the temporary nature of previous job support schemes, including the Kickstart programme during the Covid pandemic, meant that they had been less effective as reducing long-term joblessness.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: How the new guarantee would work in practice is not yet clear, with McFadden adding it would have to be "carefully" drafted.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: Although local councils have some specific legal duties, including in the areas of child protection and homelessness, duties on central government currently tend to be much broader, such as operating a "comprehensive" health service.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: Other claimants, such as those with long-term disabilities, would receive an increased amount, he added.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: Also speaking to Kuenssberg, shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said her party backed moves to reduce welfare spending.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: But she criticised the proposed legal guarantee of work support, arguing it might "sound a nice thing to do," but ministers would be better off reducing taxes and regulations on businesses to help youngsters find "real jobs".
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: She added it was "absurd" the government had increased taxes for employers in order to "subsidise things that look like jobs".
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: She added: "Just stop doing the taxing.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: From next April, eligible claimants will be offered a role after 12 months of unsuccessfully looking for work, rather 18 currently.
sentences.article_title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people

sentences.text: It is the second time that eligibility for the scheme has been widened, after the maximum age was increased from 21 to 24 earlier this year .

sentences.text: Holly Humberstone says she was having an identity crisis on a weekly basis You might know her as a pop star, endorsed by everyone from Taylor Swift to Sam Fender, but Holly Humberstone has a secret double life.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: In her spare time, the singer-songwriter is literally a cat burglar.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "We've stolen one of our neighbours' cats by accident," she laughs, in a Zoom call from her fixer-upper in New Cross, south-east London.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "He's a tiny little black cat who's come into our garden and simply chosen us." Under the slightest scrutiny, however, her story crumbles like a biscuit in a hot cup of tea.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "OK, we've been coercing him into the house with treats," she admits.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "But we're not trying to keep him.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: We literally push him out every night." Humberstone's excuse for this feline felony is that, last year, her parents sold her childhood home in Lincolnshire , external and moved to Wales  – taking her pets with them.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: One, a cat called Tsuki, had even been immortalised in the song Lucy as a confidante who listens to her problems but "never judges".
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "Oh, she knows some secrets!" laughs the singer.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "I'm so glad she can't talk." "We actually tried to bring her to London with us, but she's a countryside cat and she hated it so much.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: We had to send her to Wales where she can be free and frolic." Her parents' relocation was disruptive for the human Humberstones, too.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: Their house, a "freezing cold, falling down" property 20 minutes outside of Grantham, played a huge part in the singer's success.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: Her early EPs were all written there, inspiring the "wonky sonics" of her indie-leaning pop sound.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: The 2021 single Haunted House is even dedicated to the "friendly" spirits who inhabited the property.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "It's a place I always felt I could go back to, to remind myself of who I am," she says.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: Instead, she spent 2025 "packing up 23 years of stuff my family and I had accumulated", from her old ballet shoes and poetry books to forgotten bits of jewellery.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: The singer shared photos of her old bedroom, and the artefacts she'd rediscovered, while clearing out her parents' "haunted house" in Grantham (pictured, left).
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: The process was unsettling.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: Already grappling with the idea of leaving childhood behind, Humberstone found herself literally throwing away her past.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: I was having some sort of identity crisis almost weekly," she says.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: So she did what she's always done, and poured those feelings into her second album, Cruel World, which entered the UK charts at number four earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "Writing these songs felt like building myself a little shield and a kind of safety bubble," she says.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "There's an escapist, fantasy element to so much of the album." Maybe that's true, but Humberstone has always had the ability to locate a song's emotional core, and the lyrics on Cruel World don't disappoint.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: " To lose somebody is to know you're only human, honey, " she sings on To Love Somebody , external , soothing her elder sister as she endures an agonising break-up.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: Undeterred by that heartbreak, she throws herself headfirst into a new affair on Die Happy , external , declaring: " Hit the gas, I want it fast, want it reckless ." But the most revealing song is the closing track, Beauty Pageant , external .
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: Fragile and raw, it's the sound of Humberstone in her dressing room, addressing the woman in the mirror who'd "die for the applause" but who struggles with the impossible beauty standards imposed on female artists.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: Humberstone's biggest songs include Falling Asleep At The Wheel, The Walls Are Way Too Thin, Die Happy and Scarlett "That's a song that I wasn't really setting out to write," she confesses.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "Writing about other people often feels easier than turning the magnifying glass on yourself." The lyrics, she says, draw on a "very specific" mindset she acquired at her all-girls school in Grantham.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "It was drilled into me: You're all in competition.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: You're only rewarded if you're the best.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: And if you're not, you're worthless." The experience "really warped the way I view other girls", she says.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: Musical success made it worse.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: After winning the Brits Rising Star award in 2022 , Humberstone found herself competing with megastars, even though her music leaned towards the alternative side of pop.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "I'm a very small fish and I recognise that, but suddenly I was in meetings being compared to all these people on my label's roster, who are on a completely different scale," she says.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "It's something I really, really struggled with in the early days and it's something I've really had to unlearn." Nowadays, Humberstone has stopped benchmarking herself against her peers, recognising that the need for validation never fades.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "I don't think that there's a point I could get to, or an award that I could win, where these feelings would disappear," she says.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: The single Too Cute To Be Lonely , external is a will-they/won't-they story set at a house party.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: " Don't leave a girl upset, in such a pretty dress ," she teases the object of her affections.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: Terminally Yours takes place a couple of weeks later, when Humberstone realises she's fallen head-over-heels in love.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: " Your stupid face is my sorry fate ," she harrumphs, cross at herself.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: " For [expletive]'s sake, I'm in love ." Silver Sky, a gorgeous acoustic ballad, tells another side of the story, as she settles into her lover's arms and drifts into blissful reverie.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "I wrote that on a kind of Hail Mary trip, seeing what fell out of the air in Nashville," she reveals.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "We went over to [co-writer Maddie Diaz's] house, took a guitar into the garden and wrote Silver Sky outside, while all of these gorgeous red cardinals were singing around us.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: Humberstone admits her stage nerves have only intensified since the release of Cruel World.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "It's the proudest I've been of any of my work and, for that reason, I struggled with shows because I felt a lot of pressure to go out and deliver it to the standard that I think people are expecting.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "But on the other hand, it's totally fine if you mess up or sing a wrong note.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: People can't connect to a pop star that feels too robotic and polished.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "So maybe my strength is that vulnerability, and I need to recognise that more." That vulnerability has won Humberstone millions of fans, even if a hit single has (so far) eluded her.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: And her audience keeps growing.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: In May this year, her breakout single Falling Asleep At The Wheel was awarded a silver disc... five years after its release, indicating that her songs have staying power in an era of disposable hits.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: Astonishingly, this is news to Humberstone, who learns about the accolade during our interview.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: But it helps to clarify a thought that's been knocking around her head.
sentences.article_title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'

sentences.text: "If I'm going to be doing this for years to come, I've just got to keep making music that feels right, trusting my gut and realising there's no end point," she says.

sentences.text: Computer programming and consultancy services in particular contributed to overall growth (generic photo) ﻿The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Between July and September, the economy expanded by 0.7%, accelerating from the previous three months, official figures , external show.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: The robust growth suggests a far more resilient economy than expected over the summer, despite the impact of higher energy prices from the Iran war.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Strong growth in the services sector - the largest part of the economy, which includes non-physical goods such as consultancy services and computer programming as well as hotels and restaurants - helped boost the numbers.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Within services, computer programming registered its fastest growth for the past three years, helped by cloud computing and AI-linked spending.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: The boost from computer programming and consultancy services has been the biggest driver of growth so far this year.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Grant Fitzner, chief economist at the Office for National Statistics, said it was "possible growth could have been even stronger" if there hadn't been a war in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: But he says households may still not feel better off, and that prices might soon start to rise more quickly than wages.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: However, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the figures were "welcome news".
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: "Despite a year where events around the world have pushed up costs here at home, our economy is growing, bringing hope for the future," he said.
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey told the BBC the figures showed a "remarkable resilience" in the face of global conflicts, and hopes they "bring back confidence in Britain".
sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.article_title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years

sentences.text: Although investors have recently been concerned about slower artificial intelligence development in the US and the long term viability of AI firms' business models, businesses have continued to invest in the technologies.

sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "They've dropped all the charges." His lawyers requested a court hearing for the prosecution to formally acknowledge that they would offer no evidence, but at the Old Bailey the newly-innocent Cash struggled to find anyone interested in his story.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Cash's life has changed almost beyond recognition, he says, but he is positive about the future At every previous court appearance he had been mobbed, but the press had not been informed about this hearing.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Eventually his team found a lone BBC journalist.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I said my piece outside the Old Bailey.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: And that was a real high point.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: I felt that I could start to move on with my life." It wouldn't be that simple.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Across the city, House of Commons Speaker Lindsay Hoyle was seething.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "It is this Parliament that has been spied on," he declared.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "It is MPs' offices that have been infiltrated." There would be days of political debate and a raucous prime minister's questions where Tory leader Kemi Badenoch would claim: "This all stinks of a cover-up." "I'd been acquitted by law, but then I was traduced in Parliament," Cash says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "It was almost like I was convicted in the court of public opinion again, by people who I had worked with and trusted and that felt horrible." Today Cash's life is almost unrecognisable.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He has lost his dream job, his relationship, and his closest friend from university.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "We talked about being each other's best men," Cash says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Instead, when the friend got married last year, Cash was not even invited.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: He is also no longer in contact with Berry.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I've been applying for basic admin jobs and having trouble recently," Cash says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I'm angry and upset with how everything played out, and I do feel let down." But when asked, Cash stops short of saying he feels Berry betrayed him.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Does he think his friend was spying for the Chinese government?
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "He would have to have his time in court to defend himself," Cash answers.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "I think it'd be wrong of me to speculate and hypocritical given the speculation that I've been subject to.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: But we're no longer friends." Berry declined to comment on this story, but at the time of his acquittal said his reports "concerned economic and commercial issues widely discussed in the UK at the time and drew on information freely in the public domain".
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Like his former friend, Chris Cash is innocent in the eyes of the law, but his reputation has undoubtedly been trashed.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: Many in Parliament still think they were spies.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: And with more of the messages between these former friends now revealed, the debate over their actions could be reignited.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "It was a gruelling ordeal," Cash says.
sentences.article_title: Acquitted 'China spy' tells BBC: I was fall guy for security services but also naive

sentences.text: "But I'm a fundamentally positive person… I'm positive about what the future holds." Get in touch – politicsinvestigations@bbc.co.uk , external

sentences.text: Key services across the UK, including the NHS, GPs and schools, have been affected by a global Microsoft outage.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Pharmacies and businesses have also been hit after email and messaging services went down.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: NHS England said patients should still attend appointments unless told otherwise, while several large police forces are urging the public to call if they want to report a crime.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Microsoft said services were now gradually being restored globally after a problem caused by a higher-than-usual stress on its servers, but users could still experience disruption.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: The government said it was working closely with the firm to assess any impact on its services, while local authorities warned that some council services were being affected.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: The full extent of the impact of the outage - which is affecting Outlook, Teams and Copilot - and the time it will take to restore the systems remains unclear hours after users first reported issues.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Some 430 million people use the online tools worldwide.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: The chief executive of the NHS Alliance, which represents the healthcare system in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, said the outage was affecting some services including emails.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: NHS trusts in England were enacting measures to minimise disruption to critical services, a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Patients have been told to continue to use 999 in an emergency and otherwise contact 111 by phone or online, or their local pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Practices in Hampshire and Shropshire have told patients to phone them or come into the surgery if they have an urgent need.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: The overall impact on health services remains unclear.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Much of the NHS calendar is linked to diaries using the Microsoft system, but workflow practices differ between hospitals and trusts.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: There are anecdotal reports of c-sections being cancelled and hospitals only accepting urgent referrals - though the impact on elective treatments has yet to be confirmed.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: The GMB union's national secretary Rachel Harrison said the outage was having a "serious impact" on ambulance and NHS trusts.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: "Those who work in 111 and 999 services are unable to refer patient details in the normal way which is creating a massive backlog and has the potential for chaos," she said, though "emergency and life-threatening call outs appear to be unaffected".
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Meanwhile, police forces in England and Wales - including the Metropolitan Police, Greater Manchester Police and Police Scotland - have said online forms may be affected.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: They are urging people to call them about any time-critical by non-emergency matters.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Downing Street said it was looking to get a "full picture" of the the extent of the outage's effect on government services.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: In England, the Local Government Association warned that some services may be disrupted but plans were in place to ensure people "continue to receive the support they need".
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Because the outage affects key organisational and communication platforms that are integrated, many other workplaces have been affected.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: That has included schools, where teachers, office staff and parents have all had to navigate being unable to access key resources on calendars, emails and internal cloud servers.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: One head teacher at a primary school near Newcastle said safeguarding systems had also been affected, meaning staff were having to report concerns in person instead of logging them, while another in Cheshire said his had been forced to delay sending out termly school reports.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Universities have also suffered disruption to online systems, including tools used to submit assignments.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Some, like the University of Portsmouth and University of Aberdeen, have extended deadlines or waived late submission penalties.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Royal Mail said some of its online services were unavailable and email notifications about deliveries may be impacted, but post was still being collected and delivered as normal MPs have been unable to access their parliamentary accounts.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Microsoft and cyber-security experts have ruled out a cyber-attack being the cause of the outage.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: The tech firm said a large number of its servers had become "unexpectedly unavailable", meaning traffic was sent to the servers that remained online, putting them under strain.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: "Just like on a motorway, when you block one lane, you have to put all of the excess traffic through just, say, one or two lanes," Jake Moore, a cyber-security adviser at ESET, explained.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: "Everything goes and backs up.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: It slows down, and that's what we're seeing here." He told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that this incident should "hammer home" the need for contingency communication networks that are "independent of others".
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, we just put so much emphasis on just a few providers - so when one big one like this goes down, the knock-on effects are just huge." His sentiment was echoed by Nicky Choo, who said his cyber-security firm Mimecast used Microsoft tools but had built-in alternatives to prevent disruption.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Some workplaces are reverting to using paper or moving to alternate communication platforms like WhatsApp to keep their businesses ticking over.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: But others have been left struggling without the Microsoft tools.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Caroline Wade, who runs her own PR agency in Kent, told the BBC that the outage had caused her "huge disruption" as she was unable to send pitches and invoices.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Meanwhile, 29-year-old Georgia Young, from Staffordshire, was due to complete a house purchase today with her partner but said it had now been delayed.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: "We've waited eight months to get to this point, it seem like it's out of reach again," she said.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Dave Walker said the outage was threatening his fledgling bakery and wine bar's online pre-Christmas sales, while Stirlingshire resident Lewis Bowles said he was unable to access his tickets for a Sunday rugby match.
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Have you or your business been affected by the outage?
sentences.article_title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has signalled his support for dedicated options at the next census to allow people to define themselves as black English or Asian English.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: It comes after Liberal Democrat MP Josh Babarinde called for legislation to widen ethnicity options for respondents at the next population count, due in 2031.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: The last census, held in 2021, saw English offered within a broader white category, but without specific options for black English or Asian English.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Asked at Prime Minister's Questions whether he would support Babarinde's proposal, Burnham said he had not seen details of the plan.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: But he added: "I stand here thinking that I would want to support that bill, to directly take on the poisonous politics we've seen from some in this House".
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: "We must bring people back together.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: I am interested in working with anyone in this House who shares that aim," he added.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Burnham did not respond to a follow-up question from Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey about whether he would meet Babarinde to discuss his plan, and he did not specify whether the government would give it time for debate in Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Babarinde introduced his proposal for legislation on Tuesday, under a rule that allows MPs to propose new laws in a 10-minute speech.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Such draft laws, known as private members' bills, rarely become law without support from the government of the day but are often used by MPs to raise awareness of issues and generate media attention for policy ideas.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP Respondents to the 2021 census were asked a two-stage question about ethnicity, with options grouped under five broad ethnic headings.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: In Wales, the terms "Asian Welsh" and "Black Welsh" were listed in the broad categories themselves, and respondents were able to pick "Welsh" as an option underneath the broader white category.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: The form in England listed "English" as an option in the white ethnic category, but the only way for respondents to describe themselves as Black English or Black English was via a free-form text box.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: In Scotland, the term "Scottish Asian" appeared in the broad categories, whilst "Black Scottish" was given as an example response for the text box.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Speaking on Tuesday, Babarinde said his proposed law would introduce Black English and Asian English as specific new categories, arguing that the text box on the current form "may as well be the margin".
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Babarinde's proposal has been backed by some MPs in other parties, including Labour former deputy prime minister David Lammy and Conservative Sir James Cleverly, who quit the shadow cabinet this summer to run for London mayor.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: The Eastbourne MP has previously told the BBC he put forward his bill in the wake of comments by former Conservative home secretary Suella Braverman, who defected to Reform UK earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Braverman wrote in 2015 , external that she was British Asian but said she "cannot claim to be English" despite being born and educated in England.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: She has reaffirmed her position in recent weeks, writing on X that Englishness was "an ethnicity" and it was "not racist to say this".
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: "To say I'm English is to take a 'laissez-faire, anything-goes' attitude to ethnicity, citizenship and identity.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: It also denies me my Asian heritage," she added.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: The detailed questions asked during the census in England and Wales are set out in legislation following recommendations from the Office for National Statistics (ONS).
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: The ONS told the BBC that the Government Statistical Service has been working on a new approach to asking about ethnicity in official surveys since 2022, with an update on the work due to be published on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: That could lead to a recommendation to change the ethnicity question at the 2031 census, although the questionnaire itself is normally designed much closer to the time the census is due to take place.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: Legislation setting out the questions for the last census was published in summer 2020, ahead of it taking place in March the following year.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: The Scottish government delayed the census in Scotland until 2022 because of the Covid pandemic.
sentences.article_title: Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census

sentences.text: The UK is one of the three biggest markets for live streamed child sexual abuse in the world Former safeguarding minister Jess Phillips has joined calls from campaigners for the government to back new technology that blocks the live-streaming of child sexual abuse.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: The UK National Crime Agency has flagged the UK as the third biggest market in the world , external for live-streamed abuse, where children are sexually abused live on camera to order.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: Device-level blockers can prevent this material being filmed and viewed on smartphones, laptops and tablets in the first place, Phillips said, at the launch of a policy report in Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: Anti-abuse campaigners claim keeping the technology at device level maintains privacy and encryption.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: Civil liberties campaigners Big Brother Watch dispute this.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: The government has already legislated to demand tech firms like Apple and Google, which develop the operating systems of most smartphones used in the UK, block under-18s from taking or sharing nude images on smartphones and other devices.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: However, three-quarters of child sexual abuse material (CSA) was not self-generated but likely captured on adult devices, according to 2025 research from the Internet Watch Foundation (IWF), which works to eliminate child sexual abuse imagery online.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: Some 1.8 million men in the UK admitted to some form of online sexual offending against children, according to research from child safety institute Childlight.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: Phillips, who complained of repeated delays to work to tackle CSA when she resigned as safeguarding minister in May, is demanding action to tackle the source of the crime and reduce the number of British offenders.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: "This should be a source of national shame, and we must stop it," the Labour MP said.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: Nothing is logged, stored or sent anywhere, and the tech would work alongside encryption.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: The AI classifier has been trained against a database of known child abuse images so it can differentiate between harmless material such as children at the beach, and sexual abuse.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: Phillips said online child sexual abuse is "an issue that we did not keep control of" as legislators and now must be prioritised, at the event in Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: She was joined by survivors of online child sexual abuse, who said they should not have to beg for the removal of images of themselves being abused from the internet.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: Phil Eccles, from the National Crime Agency (NCA), said the scale of the problem was "at crisis point".
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: "This would cut off at source somebody on the UK their ability to direct a live stream for a child to be abused," he said.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: "To me, safeguarding children will always supersede the ability to prosecute.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: If we can stop that abuse we must.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: He said: "By the time the police are involved, a child has already been abused and the images and videos have gone round the globe.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: "The material has to be blocked on the phone itself, before the harm is done.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: "The government deserves real credit for committing to exactly that on children's phones.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: "I urge it now to extend that commitment to every device sold in Britain, targeted at CSA material, and to lead the world in doing so." In a sign of CSA becoming more prevalent, communications watchdog Ofcom has found almost as many offenders looking for CSA on everyday apps on the open web as on the dark web.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: John Tanagho, from the anti-trafficking organisation the International Justice Mission, highlighted how children in poorer countries were being targeted for sexual exploitation, with research showing one in every 100 Filipino children were victims.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: Legislation should explicitly limit the scans to identifying and blocking CSA material, he said, with no data shared with the government or any private companies, maintaining privacy.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: However, civil liberties campaigners Big Brother Watch warned about the possibility of innocent images being blocked or the technology being adapted for surveillance in future.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: "Effective child protection requires a stronger criminal justice response," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: "Yet police are already overwhelmed by reports of child sexual abuse, while the NCA has rightly raised concerns that eight in ten offenders convicted of possessing child abuse images avoid prison.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: "Genuine child protection requires well-resourced, targeted policing and robust enforcement of the law, not the scanning of every phone in Britain." A government spokesperson did not respond directly to the new call for CSA blockers, but said: "We are putting in place the strongest online safety laws in the world.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: "This includes preparing world-first legislation to call on the biggest technology companies to make it impossible for children to take, share or view nude images.
sentences.article_title: Former minister calls for phone tech to block live-streamed child sex abuse

sentences.text: "We will also give the police the powers they need to keep pace with criminal use of emerging technologies in order to keep our children safe." sentences.text: Cancer charities and doctors say sunbeds are linked to higher rates of melanoma and other skin cancers A watchdog has launched a crackdown on misleading sunbed adverts, warning tanning firms they must not claim their beds are safe or can treat medical conditions.
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: The Committee for Advertising Practice (CAP) said it was issuing a UK-wide enforcement notice to "send a clear message to the industry that advertisers must not downplay the risks associated with sunbed use".
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: Earlier this year, the BBC identified hundreds of social media videos claiming the beds could boost energy and treat skin conditions or mental health problems.
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: The Sunbed Association, which represents around half of the UK's tanning salons, said it fully supported action against misleading adverts, but said businesses must still be allowed to demonstrate they operate responsibly.
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: The CAP, which draws up the UK's advertising rules, said some of the claims being made by companies were potentially harmful and could discourage customers from seeking appropriate medical treatment or advice.
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: "Sunbeds carry serious health risks, including an increased risk of skin cancer," said the CAP's compliance executive James Burnett.
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: "Ads shouldn't downplay those risks or present sunbed use as a way to improve health." Cancer charities and doctors are clear about the risks of using sunbeds - and say the machines are linked to higher rates of melanoma and other skin cancers.
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: Using a bed before the age of 35 increases the risk of melanoma by 59% later in life, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: Young people are by far the biggest sunbed users in the UK - about one in seven 18-to-24-year-olds say they used one in the past year, double the average for all age groups, according to a 2025 YouGov survey.
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: Rosie Vare, health information manager at Teenage Cancer Trust, said skin cancer was one of the most common forms of the disease in young adults and she welcomed stricter enforcement of the advertising rules.
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: "We want young people to be properly informed about the risk of sunbed use and we recommend using trusted, regulated sources to find out information such as the NHS , external or cancer charities , external ," she added.
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: Earlier this year, the Advertising Standards Authority (ASA), which enforces the CAP code, banned five adverts that claimed sunbeds could help manage conditions including osteoporosis and depression.
sentences.article_title: Sunbed firms must not downplay cancer risk, says watchdog

sentences.text: It was during Patrina's illness that Declan found an outlet in the form of endurance sports, setting him on a path to his 3,800-mile (6,115km) epic cycle across the US.
sentences.article_title: 'I cycled across America in memory of my wife - I know she's proud of me'

sentences.text: "I've always been a keen runner and love to cycle, and even when she was sick Patrina would give me the green light to go off to the Mourne mountains for the day," he said.

sentences.text: "There were days when you felt like your body was just shutting down and you were sore all over, because we were spending sometimes 10 hours a day on the bikes without a break." sentences.text: "Seeing that for the first time was special.

sentences.article_title: 'I cycled across America in memory of my wife - I know she's proud of me'

sentences.text: "Cycling through the strongest winds I've ever experienced in South Dakota was probably the toughest.
sentences.article_title: 'I cycled across America in memory of my wife - I know she's proud of me'

sentences.text: But is that pricey max strength flu remedy really any better than a basic box of painkillers?
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: "The big brands have been around for a while, they've been tested, and there are adverts on the TV saying they're really good," says Prof Jayne Lawrence, head of the pharmacy division at the University of Manchester.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: "But in reality, there's very little difference.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: Personally, I'd always go for the cheaper ones - and they’ve also been tested." The trade association representing over-the-counter medicine makers says familiar brands can reassure shoppers and help them find the right product on crowded supermarket shelves.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: The medications we've highlighted all contain similar ingredients with marginal differences to their quantities.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: Cold and flu drugs fall into three broad camps: household names such as Lemsip and Sudafed, supermarket own-label alternatives and single-ingredient medicines containing paracetamol or ibuprofen.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: The difference in price can be striking.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: A packet of 16 Lemsip All-In-One Max Strength tablets retails at £7.30, more than 20 times the £0.35 cost of paracetamol pills in some supermarkets.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: Both contain 500mg of paracetamol, which doesn't treat the underlying infection but does relieve pain and can bring down a fever.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: The Lemsip version, along with many of its competitors, also contains the decongestant phenylephrine.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: It's meant to constrict leaky or swollen blood vessels in the nose which can cause congestion.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: But Lawrence says there is little evidence it works when taken as a tablet, rather than as a nasal spray, because much of the drug is broken down before it can reach the bloodstream.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: In 2024, the US drug regulator said it wanted phenylephrine removed from all cold and flu pills, saying it was simply not effective, although that proposal has yet to be finalised.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: Some cold and flu remedies contain a third active ingredient - guaifenesin - which is meant to loosen mucus in the airways.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: That sits in more of a grey area: some studies report improvements in chest congestion, while others find little or no benefit.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: A spokeswoman for Reckitt, which owns Lemsip and Nurofen, says the ingredients in its products are approved by regulators and formulated for multiple symptoms including fever, congestion and coughs.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: Many popular max strength remedies can also contain up to 65mg of caffeine per pill, about the same as a mug of instant coffee.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: As well as acting as a mild stimulant, research suggests caffeine may boost the effect of paracetamol , external and help it work slightly sooner, although any benefit is likely to be modest.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: Almost every brand can also be found as a flavoured powder to dissolve in hot water, typically costing slightly more per dose than pills or tablets.
sentences.article_title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?

sentences.text: That warm drink can be soothing and a study funded by a drug company , external found it may be absorbed into the bloodstream more quickly, but whether patients notice any major difference in their symptoms is much less certain.

sentences.text: New blood tests designed to check for multiple cancers in one go will be offered to NHS patients in some 200 GP surgeries in England as part of a trial.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The aim is to detect hard-to-diagnose abdominal cancers, including liver, ovarian and pancreatic cancer, much sooner.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: These cancers are often found only after they have spread.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The tests look for proteins or fragments of DNA in the blood that may signal cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Results could help doctors decide which patients with vague symptoms need further investigations.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: More than 20,000 patients aged 45 and over with symptoms such as pain or persistent bloating will be eligible to take part.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The government-funded trial, led by the University of Birmingham, will assess whether the tests are accurate enough for wider NHS use.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The idea of a blood test that can identify multiple cancers is not new.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: A separate NHS trial of a test called Galleri recently failed to meet its main goal of reducing diagnoses of late-stage cancers, although researchers are still assessing its potential benefits.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Prof Peter Johnson, NHS England's national clinical director for cancer, said detecting abdomen cancer early was "notoriously difficult" because symptoms can easily be mistaken for other less serious conditions.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Earlier diagnosis gives patients a much better chance of successful treatment and survival.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Around 71,000 people in England are diagnosed each year with pancreatic, stomach, liver, ovarian or bowel cancer, and nearly 35,000 die from these diseases.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The new STRIDE-RCT trial , external is about detecting bowel, small bowel, stomach, oesophageal, pancreatic, liver, bile duct and gallbladder, ovarian, endometrial, kidney, bladder and prostate cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Patients will provide one or two tubes of blood, taken at their GP practice, alongside routine tests.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Scientists will then analyse the samples for signs of cancer and, if present, may be able to pinpoint where in the body the tumour is located.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: A positive result does not automatically mean there is cancer, and a negative result is not a guaranteed all-clear.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Health secretary Yvette Cooper said she hoped simple blood tests such as these would help identify patients needing urgent investigation much sooner.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Michelle Mitchell from Cancer Research UK said: "GPs have long needed better tools to help them navigate that uncertainty by identifying which patients require further testing and this trial in England is an important step towards addressing that need."
