sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Some public health experts argued that the proposed trial raised broader questions about whether vulnerable populations in African countries were being asked to take risks that researchers would not accept in wealthier countries.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The BBC has asked the US department of health and human services for comment.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Here is what you need to know.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The study was planned at the Bandim Health Project, a research centre that has operated in Guinea-Bissau since 1978.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: It was designed to involve 14,000 newborns, with half receiving a hepatitis B vaccine shortly after birth and the other half not being given the shot .
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Bandim said the trial aimed to investigate whether the hepatitis B vaccine given at birth has broader health effects beyond preventing infection.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Previous studies in The Gambia and Guinea-Bissau have raised questions about a possible link to increased mortality.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Researchers argued that because Guinea-Bissau does not currently offer routine hepatitis B vaccinations at birth, despite WHO recommendations, they have a unique opportunity to study its effects before such vaccines are introduced in 2028.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: But critics questioned the ethics of withholding the vaccine from some babies, particularly in one of the world's poorest countries, where the infection is widespread.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The Trump administration funded the proposed study, with the CDC awarding the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) $1.6m (£1.2m) in December 2025 .
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Walter Kazadi Mulombo, the WHO representative in Guinea-Bissau, told the BBC they became concerned after receiving questions about the study and finding no publicly available protocol.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: He said the main ethical concern was that the trial would withhold an intervention already proven to protect newborns against hepatitis B.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "The vaccine has been used for more than 30 years in more than 115 countries," he said.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "A study that will withhold that intervention from other newborns is unethical." He warned that babies could be exposed to the virus during childbirth if their mothers were infected, as well as later in life.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Nearly a fifth of the population of Guinea-Bissau are infected with hepatitis B, a viral infection that affects the liver.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Those infected during infancy are particularly likely to develop chronic infections, which kill up to 25% of people, mostly through liver failure or liver cancer, according to data published in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The WHO is working with the government to bring forward the birth-dose vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "The country had been expected to add it to its routine immunisation schedule in 2028, but officials are considering introducing it in the first quarter of next year," Mulombo said.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Guinea-Bissau currently vaccinates children against hepatitis B at six weeks, which means it is less effective.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Guinea-Bissau's government prohibited hepatitis B vaccine trials involving children in January.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: At the time, it requested a team of experts from the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) to help evaluate the study.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Health Minister Quinhin Nantote said in October that the suspension remained in force and had not been overturned by the Council of Ministers after reports emerged claiming that the trial would be taking place after all.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "We were surprised to learn from media reports that the study might proceed," Nantote said.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "We are outraged because even I, as the minister responsible for this sector, was not informed." The dispute intensified after the SDU said a revised study protocol had received ethical approval "from the relevant authorities in Guinea-Bissau", which Nantote denied.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Dr Gavin Yamey, a professor of global health and public policy at Duke University in the US, criticised the proposal.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "The proposed trial reeks of neocolonialism," he told the BBC, questioning why the research was not being conducted in Denmark.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: His criticism centred on the decision to withhold a recommended vaccine from some newborns in a country where hepatitis B is widespread.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: SDU dean Jakob Grauslund said the trial had never started, no babies had been enrolled and no vaccinations administered as part of the research.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The SDU said it had received a separate, positive assessment from the university's own research ethics committee.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Grauslund said the university had sought an additional independent assessment, although Danish law did not require one.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: He added that the relevant Danish statutory research ethics bodies were unable to undertake the review.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Following the approval from the SDU's ethics committee, Grauslund decided that the project could proceed.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: He, however, stressed that this did not replace the separate authorisation required from Guinea-Bissau's authorities.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: On 19 October, Guinea-Bissau's Judicial Police searched the Bandim Health Project's facilities in the capital, Bissau, and seized a batch of hepatitis B vaccines.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Police said the batch was intended for vaccinating children but did not disclose how many doses had been seized or the specific grounds for the investigation.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: They stressed that the seizure did not, in itself, mean the vaccines were defective or unsafe.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The police have not explicitly said whether their investigation relates to the proposed trial, the importation of the vaccines or other circumstances surrounding the batch.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Grauslund said he could not comment on the seizure of the vaccines.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The proposed trial was funded by the US government at a time of significant changes to vaccine policy under President Donald Trump and Health Secretary Kennedy.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Under Kennedy's leadership, a US vaccine panel attempted to end a longstanding recommendation that all newborns receive a hepatitis B vaccine at birth, but a federal judge later blocked this, along with other changes to vaccine policy made by the Trump administration.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Critics have questioned whether the research could help support that policy shift, although the study's stated aim was to investigate potential effects of the vaccine beyond preventing infection.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Kennedy has praised the Danish researchers as "the deities of vaccine research", and cited earlier findings from their work in support of concerns about vaccine safety.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: A subsequent study by some of the same researchers, however, found no evidence of the previously reported effect.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: There is no evidence that the proposed trial was designed to justify a change in US policy.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Too many university students can use AI to complete assessments without staff finding out, the higher education regulator in England has said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The Office for Students (OfS) said "a significant proportion" of assessments are unsupervised and many can be completed to a high standard with AI, sometimes in minutes.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said this posed a "significant risk" to their credibility, and closed-book and practical exams were the most effective forms of assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK said many institutions had "made substantial changes" to make assessments "AI-proof".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities that do not meet OfS quality standards could soon be banned from charging increased tuition fees or have caps imposed on their student numbers, under proposals that are now being consulted on.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The new research from the OfS and Advance HE, a charity that gives awards for teaching excellence, is based on the views of 244 higher education staff and 91 students from at least 127 universities.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said "a significant proportion of assessments" were in "unsupervised, non-controlled formats where AI can be accessed by students completing them".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "Many of these can be completed to a high standard using AI tools with limited engagement from students," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It also concluded it was "frequently possible" for students to use AI "in ways that cannot be reliably detected".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Unsupervised assessment can include coursework, but also remote online exams.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: They were rolled out widely during Covid, and research from Swansea University , external last year suggests 93 universities in the UK still use them in some form.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Josh Fleming, director of strategy and delivery at the OfS, said there were "fantastic" examples of universities seizing opportunities presented by AI, but there should be "far greater use of AI-free assessment".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It also presents a generational risk to the system as it stands, threatening to undermine students' learning and institutions' ability to assess them," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Kathryn Harrison-Graves, deputy chief executive at Advance HE, said students wanted "greater clarity about what is expected of them" but staff had "varying levels of confidence and support".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Some staff, meanwhile, were receiving lots of assignments that looked the same, and did not think their institution's assessments were "fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Other staff described a "polarised atmosphere" between students who used AI and other "conscientious objectors" who avoided it on environmental and other grounds.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The research said AI literacy for students was important during and after university, and some institutions were clearly communicating to students where AI can and cannot be used in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: But it said there was "an urgent need" to ensure that remote or "non-secure" assessments "maintain their validity despite the availability of AI tools, meaning they effectively assess the knowledge and skills they are designed to measure".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "If it becomes possible to complete an assessment using AI without the knowledge and skills being tested, the assessment should be replaced," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK, which represents more than 140 institutions, said universities were "making significant progress" adapting to AI.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "There is further to go but many have made substantial changes to how they assess students.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: This includes more in-person exams, presentations, vivas, process-based assessment and assessments that integrate AI in a controlled way," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It's time to get rid of the outdated methods, that have been kept around in the name of tradition, and instead encourage the innovative practice we see across the sector, co-designed with students based on what they want from higher education," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Pupils will not be allowed access to their phones at all during the school day under stricter government guidance in England.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Statutory guidance came into force in June, making schools and trusts legally responsible for being phone-free throughout the day.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Ministers now say changes to that guidance will go beyond the current "no see, no hear" policies in place in some schools - where phones can remain in pupils' bags if they are not seen or heard - when it comes into force from September 2027.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: But head teachers' unions said schools would struggle to implement stricter new policies without additional funding from government.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell said the government's "clear message" to parents and pupils was that "school is for learning and friendship, not scrolling".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Access to phones "risks pulling children away from their learning and from each other", the government said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Schools will be able to decide how to follow the guidance.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Some schools have invested in sealed pouches or secure lockers.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Others collect phones at the start of the day, or have prohibited them from sites altogether.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Powell said such policies could achieve a "whole-school culture change" - and that was "what we want to see happening everywhere".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Karl Harrison, head teacher at Burnage Academy for Boys in Manchester, told the programme the school had spent £20,000 to bring in a system of metal detectors and phone pouches to prevent pupils from accessing their phones.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: While some felt their freedom had gone, locking phones away had increased how much pupils socialised at school, he said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "People now can talk to each other, instead of scrolling on a device," he said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: But he said the more robust measures recommended under the new guidance would "come at a cost".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said the latest guidance "does at least provide some clarity", but added that school leaders "cannot simply make mobile phones disappear".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "If all schools are going to be expected to have lockable pouches or other secure storage facilities for every pupil, the cost involved will be very significant indeed," he said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "This is not feasible unless the government puts in the funding required to meet these costs." Responding to questions about funding, Powell told BBC Breakfast that she wanted heads to have the autonomy to implement the policies that work best for their schools.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Dame Rachel de Souza, Children's Commissioner for England, said she welcomed strong action to stop phones distracting pupils and disrupting the school day.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Charlotte Ashton, co-founder of campaign group of Generation Focus, similarly welcomed the changes, saying "no see, no hear" policies were not working and pupils were still "TikToking in the toilets".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "Ultimately, we need to get to a point where it's not normal for every single child to have a personal internet-enabled device in their pockets with them 24/7," she said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: A smartphone ban in English schools is coming into force.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Parents want to ban smartphones in schools, but there's one reason they're worried Shadow Education Secretary Laura Trott said she was "delighted that Labour have finally listened to us and agreed to properly ban smartphones in schools".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: She said it was also the "right thing to do" to have a review of safety standards around the technology used in schools, which the government has also announced on the back of calls for improved guidance .
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: But she criticised what she called a lack of "joined up thinking" over what new tech was being allowed in classrooms.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Because education is devolved, the approach to phones in schools varies across the UK.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: In Scotland , external , the government has said it will introduce a new law to restrict the personal use of phones in schools, and launched a consultation on the issue over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: In Wales , external , the Senedd recently voted against a motion to introduce a national statutory ban on phones in classrooms.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: The Welsh government launched a 12-week consultation in September, which it says will shape its guidance to support schools in developing a mobile phone policy.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Schools are still encouraged to restrict the use of phones during the school day, but heads have flexibility over how to implement their own rules.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: And in Northern Ireland , Education Minister Paul Givan launched a 12-week consultation in August on whether to ban mobile phones from schools by law, calling for "a stronger and more consistent approach across our education system".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Rules around phones in schools are separate from the UK's upcoming ban on social media for under-16s, due to be introduced in March.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Children will be barred from accessing platforms like Instagram, Snapchat and TikTok.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Vinted and eBay could also be included in the list of platforms set to be banned, the culture secretary has said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.

sentences.text: The government has warned some schools start teaching GCSEs in the first year of secondary school Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught in England.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The government plans to make Key Stage 3 a more distinct education phase, urging schools to focus less on exams and more on a "richer, more engaging" experience.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The changes come in response to two reviews that found pupils were increasingly becoming disengaged in their early teenage years, affecting attendance and achievement, the Department for Education (DfE) said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The move will mark a reversal of the approach taken by the previous Conservative government to focus the first three years of secondary school on core subjects and on doing well in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Former Education Secretary Michael Gove prioritised English, maths and science, while raising grade boundaries, making exams harder and limiting resits.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: He also made GCSEs linear, meaning they are sat all in one go at the end of Year 11 instead of over the course of Key Stage 4.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: These reforms meant teachers started preparing pupils for exams at an earlier stage at the expense of teaching unexamined parts of their subject.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The DfE has pledged a "more engaging offer" in subjects like drama, PE, music and languages, which have seen a decline in students taking them, when it publishes its new curriculum later this year.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: It says persistent absence nearly doubles among pupils between Year 6 and Year 9.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The department pointed to a recent survey commissioned by the International Baccalaureate that found GCSE prep dominated Key Stage 3 learning in England, with 57% of teachers saying it was the leading influence on the curriculum.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "The pressures of GCSEs and an overcrowded curriculum are resulting in too many children receiving a narrower offer during Key Stage 3 and being rushed towards exams without grasping the fundamentals or developing deeper understanding," Powell said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "I'm putting a stop to that." A 2015 Ofsted report suggested that Key Stage 3 may be "wasted years", echoing the view at the time that pupils aged 11-14 lacked a clear motivation to work hard.

sentences.text: Several universities in England have only been using below-average salaries in examples of student loan repayments on their websites, the BBC has found.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Treasury Committee chair Dame Meg Hillier, who led a recent inquiry into student loans, said some information about repayments was "misleading", including one instance where they were compared to the "cost of a daily coffee".

sentences.text: She also said the Department for Education (DfE) must include higher-salary examples on its own website, too.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The DfE said it would review the information it provides, while universities said their websites referred to government information and would be reviewed where necessary.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Student loan repayments are tied to earnings, so the more you earn, the more you repay every month - and graduates generally go on to earn more than non-graduates.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Current and prospective students in England take out Plan 5 loans to pay for their tuition fees and living costs.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: They repay 9% of anything they earn over £25,000 for 40 years, or until the loan is paid off.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The BBC looked at publicly available information on more than 110 university websites in England and found cases of inaccurate information about the salary at which they start repaying and the length of time they repay for.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: It also found that 12 universities only gave students worked examples of repayments based on earnings that are less than the UK average, which is £39,039.

sentences.text: The DfE website also only gives examples of monthly repayments for people earning up to £38,400 on other student loan plans, but does not include any real-world repayment examples for Plan 5 students.

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We've had trees die," he added.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: Meanwhile, senior gardener at High Beeches near Haywards Heath, Elliot Chandler, said some rhododendrons had died off this year.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: "That's probably going to continue," he said.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: "We'll do what we can for the plants...but if they're not surviving, then we need to plant different things.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: "That's the only way we can really maintain the garden and keep it full of interest and flowers." This year's heat and lack of rainfall were unprecedented Joe Whelan, head gardener at Nymans in Handcross, warned another year of drought could be "quite detrimental" on larger, more mature trees.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: The gardeners said planting a greater diversity of species will be key to climate resilience, with plants from North America, southeastern Europe, central Asia, South Korea and Japan potentially faring better in future.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: Chandler added it will not be a case of ripping out old plants and planting new species "in one go" but rather a gradual change over time with a "really diverse mix of things".
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: Whelan said it will be difficult to predict what will do well in the future.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: It will be about "experimenting and accepting that some things probably aren't going to make it", he continued.
sentences.article_title: Extreme weather leaves gardeners hedging their bets

sentences.text: The National Trust hopes to create new wildlife habitats to attract wildlife including water vole and turtle doves A 370-acre (150-hectare) area of land on the edge of Cambridge has been returned to the care of the National Trust - for the first time in 60 years.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: The area - known as Northfield - runs alongside the opposite side of Quy Road towards Bottisham, seven miles (11km) from the city and close to Anglesey Abbey.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: The National Trust hopes to restore the natural site to create new wildlife habitats and improve community access to green space.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: Northfield is a rich natural site with a distinctive fen-edge landscape where low-lying fenland meets the higher chalk ridge Northfield has been acquired by the trust for the first time since the 1960s, following an agreement with the tenants.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: The site has a rich natural and cultural heritage as well as a chalk stream, with the trust describing the area as "a distinctive fen-edge landscape where low-lying fenland meets the higher chalk ridge".
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: There is evidence of human activity on the site stretching back thousands of years including the Roman period.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: The National Trust said it hoped that, over time, species such as harvest mice, water voles and turtle doves would benefit.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: Northfield is the first project within the trust's new masterplan for the area, which forms part of a wider Wicken Fen Vision and long-term initiative to "create a more connected and resilient landscape for wildlife and people stretching from Wicken Fen to the edge of Cambridge".
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: Community drop-in sessions about the vision , external will be held between Saturday 21 November and Friday 27 November.
sentences.article_title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration

sentences.text: Feedback will be used to help inform the next stage of planning before proposals are developed during 2027.

sentences.article_title: Toby Jones stars in film about UK Mars mission

sentences.text: Swans and ducks have enjoyed the wetland reserve at Slimbridge for 80 years Most people know rainforests are vital in the fight against climate change, but now scientists say wetlands could be even more important.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Saltmarshes, mangrove swamps and wetlands can absorb carbon "four times faster than trees", according to the charity the Wildfowl and Wetlands Trust (WWT).
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Celebrating 80 years since WWT's first wetland bird reserve was founded at Slimbridge, in Gloucestershire, the charity's leaders have called for one million hectares of wetlands to be restored across the world.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Sarah Fowler, CEO of WWT, said: "They are mood-boosting, flood-buffering, water-purifying, incredible habitats.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: But we have lost 85% of the world's wetlands." Sir Peter Scott feeds migrating swans and geese at Slimbridge in 1947, with Desmond Hawkins, BBC features producer from Bristol WWT now runs 10 wetland bird reserves across the UK.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Many people come to enjoy the swans, geese, flamingoes and migrating wildfowl, but do not realise how powerful these habitats can be in soaking up carbon and slowing down climate change.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: So how vital are wetlands for birds, and how powerful can they be in the fight against climate change?
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: This video can not be played The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change In November 1946, a naturalist called Peter Scott came to a wild marshy area on the banks of the River Severn, near Slimbridge.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: He was drawn by the thousands of migrating geese and swans that flew thousands of miles from the Russian Arctic to spend the winter here on the mudflats and marshes.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Captivated, Scott settled in a small cottage and later built a house right on a lake, with a huge window to watch the wildfowl.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: He dug lakes and connecting channels, built hides and even towers to watch the birds without disturbing them.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Over the years, the reserve grew and became home to thousands of ducks, swans , geese as well as the migrating wildfowl.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Sir Peter Scott with the first nine Nēnē geese he hand-reared at Slimbridge in 1952 "He really was a pioneer in conservation," said Chris Moore, a historian of Slimbridge and author of Peter Scott and the Birth of Modern Conservation.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: As well as creating a safe haven for endangered species, Scott was a vigorous campaigner for nature.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: He led the fight to stop commercial whaling, presented some of the BBC's first natural history programmes called live from Slimbridge, and helped set up WWF, the World Wildlife Fund.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: In 1973 Sir Peter Scott became the first person to be knighted for conservation work.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Moore explained: "Scott was talking about the impact that man was having on the natural world, long before we started talking about climate change and global warming.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "David Attenborough called him the Patron Saint of Conservation, and I think that is more than deserved," Moore added.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Electrical items caused fatal fire, inquest hears Councillor admits harassing bar owner Residents protest against plans for  greenbelt homes One of Scott's typically ambitious projects was to save the Hawaiian Goose, or Nēnē.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Unique to the Pacific islands, the Nēnē was hit hard by road building and development.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: By 1949 barely 24 birds remained.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Scott heard of its plight, and asked Hawaiian authorities to send a few geese to Slimbridge where he hand-reared them.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "Unfortunately they sent us two females," chuckled Enid Cole, a WWT volunteer at Slimbridge.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "Peter asked them for a gander - 'It would help', he said." Nine chicks were later born, and hand-raised successfully to adulthood at Slimbridge.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Dave Harvey helped to feed the Nēnē geese at Slimbridge Today there are more than 3,000 Nēnē geese, most of them living peacefully on Hawaiian golf courses.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: But a handful still live at Slimbridge, where Enid Cole and her friends hand feed them lettuce every day.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "It's a marvelous project, and typical of Sir Peter," Enid smiled.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Over the last 80 years, the teams at Slimbridge have hand-reared several other species, including the Common Crane and the world's rarest diving duck, the Madagascan Pochard.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: It was while they were working to save the Madagascan Pochard that they realised how vital the wetland habitats were.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "We realised that to save that species, we had to bring the wetland back," explained Sarah Fowler, WWT's chief executive.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: And yet, as Fowler explained, "40% of the world's species rely on wetland habitats for survival".
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: What started at Slimbridge has spread to 10 wetland reserves across the UK with the charity now working with local councils to restore wetlands, even in small city areas.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Wetlands are 'mood-boosting, flood buffering habitats' said Sarah Fowler, Chief Executive of WWT The Wetlands Charity A scheme in Bristol has seen small floating islands of wetland plants moored in the city's harbour.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Across the world, they are campaigning to restore one million hectares of lost wetland, partly to provide safe habitats for endangered species but also because wetlands help absorb carbon far quicker than even forests.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "Salt marshes bury carbon," said Fowler.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "Every time the big tides go over them, the plants that have grown up in the salt marsh get buried.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Those plants are full of carbon, so they are a massive carbon sink.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: "And the brilliant thing about salt marshes is they do this four times faster than trees.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: Wetlands are vital in our fight against climate change, and we must restore them." What started 80 years ago as a bird reserve on the banks of a river in Gloucestershire has grown into a global campaign to restore wetlands, which they call the "soggy secret weapon" against climate change.
sentences.article_title: The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

sentences.text: This video can not be played What happened overnight with the Microsoft global outage?
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: At least 74 countries were affected by the Microsoft outage which was detected after midday US Eastern Time (17:00 GMT) on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: Microsoft 365 Services, including Teams, Outlook and artificial intelligence software Copilot, all experienced "connectivity problems", the company said.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: As of early Friday afternoon (GMT), Microsoft was reporting improvements, with email queues "significantly reduced and approaching normal levels".
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: From city governments in the US to Australian spy agencies, the disruption was widespread.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: Here is what happened around the world.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: In the US , staff with the House of Representatives told Politico , external their work had been halted by the outage.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: "We all use Outlook, that's our life, everything is there, our calendar is there, our boss's calendar, so it has been a challenge … with no access to our Bible," one House staff member said.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: "There goes a day of legislative work." Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic both reported problems.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: OpenAI, which makes ChatGPT, said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which caused some tools not to work as expected.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: Courts from Los Angeles to Texas also warned that communications might be delayed.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: Electric truck maker Workhorse Group, which was expected to report third-quarter results on 12 November, rescheduled to 16 November, citing business disruptions caused by the outage.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: Meanwhile, officials in some US cities encouraged citizens to call local offices and agencies where needed instead of using email.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: The City of Austin in Texas account posted on X early on Friday: "Due to an ongoing Microsoft Outlook outage, City of Austin employees cannot receive or send emails at this time.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: "City phone lines remain operational, and 911 Emergency services are not impacted." In Canada , a healthcare network running several hospitals in Toronto declared a "code grey", indicating an infrastructure failure.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: The company, Unity Health Toronto, said its teams were having trouble sending or receiving email but that patient care was not affected.
sentences.article_title: Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

sentences.text: A jury at Southwark Crown Court found Russell Brand guilty of one count of rape and three of sexual assault This week, the dark side of television has come crashing into the open.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: On Monday, disgraced entertainer Russell Brand was jailed for rape and sexual assault.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: Twenty-four hours later, author and comedian David Walliams was unmasked and accused of preying on young women.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: By Friday the Metropolitan Police had launched an investigation into further allegations about him.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: Also in the last week, Married at First Sight UK has been cancelled following allegations of rape on the hit TV show.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: These are all very different stories, but each can be seen as a major reckoning with abuse of power and culture in the industry.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: So why is this all happening now?
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: In reality, the glut of recent days is something of a coincidence.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: All these revelations began with journalistic investigations that started years ago.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: From my own experience - including in my Panorama on Married at First Sight UK - I know investigations typically take a very long time to reach a conclusion, from initial tip-off, to evidence-gathering, corroboration, getting responses, and eventually reporting.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: "The truth is, these stories have a long build up.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: It can be incredibly difficult to get [them] in the papers," Sunday Times columnist Hadley Freeman told me.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: In the case of Brand, there was then a police investigation too, before an outcome was reached in court.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: Together these stories represent the consequences of changes that began years ago, rather than a sudden cultural shift in the entertainment industry.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: It should also be said that Walliams denies the allegations against him .
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: The men accused of rape and sexual misconduct on MAFS UK have also denied all the allegations.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: What has changed is that women (because it almost always is women) have seen others speaking up - which, according to broadcaster Kirsty Wark, has given them "courage to do the same".
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: She describes those who have come forward as "beyond brave".
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: When looking at what’s driving more women to speak up, much can be traced back to the revelations about Harvey Weinstein and the #MeToo movement.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: It changed the perception of whether victims would be believed.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: In the past, women alleging this sort of behaviour faced barriers - being seen as opportunistic, fearing retaliation, believing they might be the only one.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: Now, there can be a snowball effect.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: Once one, two or three come forward, that prompts others to revisit their experiences - which they may have dismissed or subdued.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: "There is more of a sense that you will now be listened to," said Freeman.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: It's also clear that when women see action taken, it can encourage others to speak up as well - as it helps counter the widely-held assumption that reporting abuse results in nothing.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: But Freeman noted it was heartening to hear the judge’s remarks in summing up the case - which have also been widely shared by women online and praised for dispelling rape myths.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.text: When Mr Justice Bennathan sentenced Brand to ten-and-a-half years, he told him: "Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say no." "I think attitudes have changed,” said Freeman.
sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.article_title: Brand, Walliams and MAFS: Is this a reckoning for the entertainment industry?

sentences.article_title: Hundreds of IDF investigations into killings still have no public outcome, BBC Verify finds

sentences.text: This was not an exhaustive search, and it is likely that there are more investigations into incidents of harm that were not captured in our search.
